pi.name: Anuj Kumar
pi.title: Professor of Molecular, Cellular, and Developmental Biology
pi.bio: Anuj Kumar earned his Ph.D. in Biomedical Sciences from Wright State University and completed postdoctoral training at Yale University in Michael Snyder's laboratory, where he held American Cancer Society Postdoctoral and Leslie Warner fellowships. At the University of Michigan he has been named a Biological Scholar, a March of Dimes Basil O'Connor Scholar, and an American Cancer Society Research Scholar, and he serves on the Faculty of 1000 (Genomics section). His lab uses functional genomics, proteomics, genetics, cell biology, and biochemistry in budding yeast and Candida albicans to study signaling pathways underlying eukaryotic cell growth, particularly the pseudohyphal growth transition.

description: The Kumar Lab applies functional genomics, proteomics, genetics, cell biology, and biochemistry to probe central signaling pathways underlying eukaryotic cell growth and function. A major focus is the transition of yeast cells from unicellular to filamentous (pseudohyphal) growth, a nutrient-responsive developmental program related to the virulence of pathogenic fungi. The lab studies ERK/MAPK and AMP-activated kinase (Snf1) signaling, uses quantitative phosphoproteomics by mass spectrometry to map kinase networks, examines the regulation of P-bodies and stress granules, and investigates metabolic messengers such as inositol polyphosphates in developmental contexts. Work is carried out in Saccharomyces cerevisiae and the human fungal pathogen Candida albicans, including studies of Candida biofilm rheology.

areas.title: Proteomic analysis of kinase signaling
areas.summary: Studies how yeast cells respond to nutritional and environmental stress through protein kinase signaling, including how the kinase Sks1p integrates nitrogen and glucose stress signals, and the relevance of these networks to Candida albicans.

areas.title: Metabolic signaling in yeast pseudohyphal growth
areas.summary: Examines how the Snf1p/AMP-activated kinase regulates morphological transitions and energy homeostasis; the lab showed that Snf1p phosphorylates the inositol polyphosphate kinase Kcs1p, linking nutrient availability to cell growth.

areas.title: Amyloid biology and yeast filamentous growth
areas.summary: Explores functional amyloid structures in fungal adhesins, finding that nearly 90 percent of identified adhesins contain sequences with high amyloid-forming potential, and developed a Flo11-based surface display system for studying amyloid aggregation.

areas.title: Large-scale analysis of the yeast kinome during filamentous growth
areas.summary: A systematic screen of yeast kinases revealed five kinases that relocalize to the nucleus during filamentous growth, forming an interdependent, stress-responsive regulatory network.
